<result>Both requests are in review. Final report:

## Root cause (file:line)
`framework/render/render_surfaces.zig` `Feed.closeFFmpeg` (was :482-492): it deinitialized the pipe reader, then called `std.process.Child.kill(io)` on the **frame thread**. Zig 0.16's `childKillPosix` (toolchain `lib/std/Io/Threaded.zig:15320`) is **one SIGTERM + an uncancelable blocking wait4 retry loop**. ffmpeg installs handlers via `signal()` (= SA_RESTART), so while blocked writing a 3.6MB raw frame into the now-undrained 64KB pipe — or restarting a V4L2 ioctl — the lone SIGTERM never interrupts it; ffmpeg never exits; the frame thread parks in wait4 **forever**. SDL converts SIGTERM into an SDL_QUIT event that only that frozen thread could pump — hence plain `kill` ignored, `kill -9` required. Every teardown (camera switch, tab leave, app quit) funnels here, with any camera. Same hazard existed in `killSubprocesses` (qemu/app) and `ChildMonitor.deinit` (Xvfb). I reproduced it standalone: the old path hangs indefinitely (timeout exit 124); the rest of the pipeline (mailbox submit/poll, MultiReader zero-timeout pipe poll, enumeration) was verified genuinely non-blocking against the real 0.16 std source.

## What changed (commit 15368781b)
- **New `framework/render/child_teardown.zig`** — the frame thread never waits on a child: synchronous SIGKILL via the platform `kill` utility (the repo's ruled signal boundary; bounded by kill(1) itself, never by the child), then the reap runs on a detached `std.Io.Group` task. A D-state child strands only that task. `render_surfaces.deinit` cancels (never awaits) the reaper group, so shutdown can't block either. Applied to ffmpeg, qemu, app, and Xvfb teardown.
- **First-frame watchdog + self-heal**: a device that opens but never streams (OBS before "Start Virtual Camera") fails LOUDLY after 10s ("camera feed FAILED: no frames from the device within 10s...") instead of an eternal black square, and paint retries the errored feed on a 10s cooldown — it heals itself once the camera starts streaming.
- **No orphaned camera locks**: ffmpeg now spawns under `setpriv --pdeathsig KILL`.
- **Loud failures**: `-loglevel error -nostats` + inherited stderr — a camera that can't open prints why.
- **Pose-input gate**: `latestCpuFrame` returns null (JS sees `no live frame`) until one real frame landed; buffer zeroed — inference can never read uninitialized bytes.

## Verification and honest limits
`zig build test-child-teardown` 2/2 PASS — reproduces the exact freeze state (SIGTERM-immune child blocked on a full pipe) and pins teardown <2s; the old `Child.kill` provably hangs in the same scenario (negative control, exit 124). pose-mailbox 3/3, video-devices 3/3, `SHIP_RUN_PACKAGE=0 tools/rjit ship editor` clean, `tools/rjit shot editor --route /play` PASS (`.../scratchpad/webcam_fix_shot.png`). **Limit**: no /dev/video device exists here, so the live end-to-end (real frames → pose overlay) wasn't exercised; the freeze mechanism itself was reproduced and fixed at the process level.

## Your OBS test script
1. In OBS: **Start Virtual Camera**. Run `./tools/rjit dev editor`, open Globals → Animation.
2. Pick the OBS camera in the top-right picker. Expect within a few seconds: video in the left pane; console lines `[render] FFmpeg capture started (1280x720)` then `[render] first GPU upload for backend=ffmpeg ...`; overlay dots + `tracking · N/17 keypoints` once you're in frame.
3. **Switch between all cameras a few times, leave the tab, come back** — this is what froze before. The app must stay responsive throughout.
4. Failure behavior to expect (not a freeze): with the virtual camera NOT started, ~10s after selecting it you get `[render] camera feed "..." FAILED: no frames from the device within 10s — is the camera streaming? (OBS: Start Virtual Camera)`, the UI shows `no live frame`, and it auto-recovers ~10-20s after you start the virtual camera (`[render] retrying errored camera feed ...`).
5. Close the app normally — it must exit on its own; plain `kill <pid>` must also work now.</result>
